Autocorrelation of the residuals within groups

Source: R/corStruct.R
corStruct.Rd

Correlation structures for the residuals of the observations of a curve over time (or in space), for the correlation argument of gcTMB, with the same arguments and the same parameterisation as corAR1, corCAR1, corExp and corGaus of the package nlme (whose objects gcTMB also accepts).

Usage

corAR1(value = 0, form = ~1, fixed = FALSE)

corCAR1(value = 0.2, form = ~1, fixed = FALSE)

corExp(
  value = numeric(0),
  form = ~1,
  nugget = FALSE,
  metric = c("euclidean", "maximum", "manhattan"),
  fixed = FALSE
)

corGaus(
  value = numeric(0),
  form = ~1,
  nugget = FALSE,
  metric = c("euclidean", "maximum", "manhattan"),
  fixed = FALSE
)

Arguments

value

Numeric. The starting value of the parameters, or their values with fixed=TRUE: rho, between -1 and 1 (default 0) for corAR1 and between 0 and 1 (default 0.2) for corCAR1; for corExp and corGaus the range, or with a nugget the range and the nugget (default: see Details)

form

One-sided formula. The time covariate (or the position variables, ~ x + y | group, for corExp and corGaus) and the grouping factor, ~ time | group. Without a grouping factor, the residuals of all observations form a single series when the model has no random effects, and are grouped by the innermost grouping factor of the random effects (the one with most levels) otherwise, as in nlme::lme. Without a time covariate (~ 1 or ~ 1 | group), the times are the positions of the observations within their group.

fixed

Logical. If TRUE, the parameters are fixed at value and not estimated

nugget

Logical. If TRUE, the spatial structure has a nugget

metric

Character. The distance between positions of several variables: "euclidean" (default), "maximum" or "manhattan", as in dist; all give |t - s| for a single time covariate

Value

An object of class c("corAR1", "corStruct") or c("corCAR1", "corStruct"): value on the unconstrained scale of nlme, log((1 + rho)/(1 - rho)) for AR(1) and log(rho/(1 - rho)) for CAR(1), with the attributes formula and fixed; or of class c("corExp", "corSpatial", "corStruct") or c("corGaus", "corSpatial", "corStruct"): value on the natural scale, as in nlme, with the attributes formula, nugget, metric and fixed.

Details

The residuals of different groups are independent. Within a group, the residuals e are stationary, with the residual variance sigma^2 of the model (sigma^2/w for weights w). For corAR1 and corCAR1, the correlation is $$cor(e_s, e_t) = rho^{|t - s|},$$ with rho the correlation of residuals one unit of time apart (Zuur et al., 2009, Section 6.1; Pinheiro and Bates, 2000, Section 5.3):

  • corAR1: the autoregressive process of order 1 at integer times (positions), with -1 < rho < 1; gaps in the times are allowed, e.g. measurements every second day with form = ~ day | ID and a day without measurement, with the correlation rho^2 across a gap of two days. Without a time covariate (form = ~ 1 | ID), the time is the position of the observation within its group, in the order of the data;

  • corCAR1: the continuous-time autoregressive process of order 1, for times that need not be integers and unequally spaced observations, with 0 < rho < 1.

The times must be unique within a group. As the process is Markov, the likelihood is the product of the density of the first residual of each group and the conditional densities of each residual given the previous one, normal with mean rho^dt e_prev and variance sigma^2 (1 - rho^(2 dt)) for the time dt between them, which is exact and linear in the number of observations.

The spatial structures corExp and corGaus give the correlation as a function of the distance d between the positions of two observations of a group, with a range r > 0 and, with nugget=TRUE, a nugget 0 < n < 1 (n = 0 otherwise):

  • corExp: \(cor = (1 - n) \exp(-d/r)\);

  • corGaus: \(cor = (1 - n) \exp(-(d/r)^2)\).

The position is the time covariate (~ time | group), with d the time between the observations, or several covariates (~ x + y | group), with d the distance of metric. Without a nugget, corExp in time is corCAR1 with rho = exp(-1/r). The nugget is the part of the residual variance that is independent between observations, such as measurement error, besides the correlated deviations of the process (Diggle, 1988); with it, observations at the same position are allowed. The residuals of a group are multivariate normal with this correlation matrix, so the time of a fit grows with the cube of the number of observations per group. As in nlme, the default starting value of the range is 90\

The estimated parameters are in coef(fit) as cor_par:AR1 or cor_par:CAR1, or cor_par:range and cor_par:nugget, on the unconstrained scale of nlme (coef of an nlme corStruct): the logit link log(rho/(1 - rho)) for CAR(1), and log((1 + rho)/(1 - rho)), the logit of (1 + rho)/2, for AR(1), whose rho lies between -1 and 1; log(r) for the range and log(n/(1 - n)) for the nugget. Wald intervals are computed on this scale and transformed back. corpars gives rho (or the range and nugget), and confint(fit, parm="cor_par:CAR1") an interval for rho. If nlme is attached after gcTMB, its constructors mask these; gcTMB accepts their objects, and gcTMB's correlation structures can be passed to nlme::gls, nlme::gnls, nlme::lme and nlme::nlme.

References

Diggle, P.J. (1988). An approach to the analysis of repeated measurements. Biometrics 44, 959-971.

Pinheiro, J.C. and Bates, D.M. (2000). Mixed-Effects Models in S and S-PLUS. Springer, New York.

Zuur, A.F., Ieno, E.N., Walker, N.J., Saveliev, A.A. and Smith, G.M. (2009). Mixed Effects Models and Extensions in Ecology with R. Springer, New York.

See also

gcTMB, corpars for the estimate of rho, and residuals(fit, type="normalized") for residuals that are independent under the model.

Examples

FabaHeights25$trt <- factor(FabaHeights25$Treatment)
fit <- gcTMB(Height ~ DAS, fform=b1 + b2 ~ trt, rform=b1 + b2 ~ 1 | Plant_ID, data=FabaHeights25,
             correlation=corCAR1(form=~ DAS | Plant_ID))
corpars(fit)
#>       rho 
#> 0.9593852 
# spatial correlation between neighbouring trees of a plot, with a nugget (independent
# measurement error), on five of the plots
pines <- droplevels(subset(PineHeightDiameter, Plot %in% 1:5))
fitn <- gcTMB(Height ~ DBH, rform=b1 ~ 1 | Plot, data=pines, model="chapmanrichards",
              correlation=corExp(form=~ X + Y | Plot, nugget=TRUE))
corpars(fitn)
#>     range    nugget 
#> 8.4016652 0.2542902
